stemMd:
Some accounts describe a scientific model as a miniature copy of reality. A model, however, often succeeds because it deliberately leaves things out. By isolating a few relationships, it can make a mechanism easier to test, even though the resulting representation is visibly incomplete.

The text primarily serves to

options.label: A
options.textMd: qualify a familiar description of models by explaining the value of selective simplification.

options.label: B
options.textMd: provide a history of miniature manufacturing.

options.label: C
options.textMd: argue that incomplete models are always inaccurate in every respect.

options.label: D
options.textMd: claim that scientists should never test mechanisms.

explanationMd: The first sentence introduces a common account, and however signals a correction. The remaining explanation shows why omission can be purposeful and useful rather than merely a defect.

distractorRationale.c: The text describes how incompleteness can aid testing.
distractorRationale.d: Testing is presented as a benefit.
distractorRationale.b: The miniature copy is a conceptual description, not the topic of a history.
